summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3, AlmaLinux 9.6, MariaDB 10.5 with galera provider from AppStream). Verified multi-master write/read replication across all members, verified continued availability with one member stopped (quorum preserved, size 2), and verified automatic resync (IST) when the stopped member returned (rejoined, size 3, Synced, and recovered the write made while it was down). Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes: baseline captured, one node rebooted at a time via `systemctl reboot`, boot_id verified changed on each, and full cluster health/data verified recovered before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes (AlmaLinux 9.6), confirmed no MariaDB pre-installed
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on all 3 nodes (node1 was initially missed, then fixed)
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera packages via dnf on all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all 3 nodes
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_on=ON, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, per-node wsrep_node_name/wsrep_node_address, wsrep_sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, enabled mariadb service
Set root password via ALTER USER on node1 (generated with openssl/urandom, stored only in /tmp files, propagated via SST)
Started/enabled mariadb on node2 and node3, both joined via SST, cluster_size=3, Synced on all nodes
Wired cluster SSH keys (CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY) to move the root password file between nodes for verification
Verified multi-master replication: insert on node1 visible on node2/node3; insert on node3 visible on node1/node2
Stopped mariadb on node2, confirmed cluster_size=2 and write availability/replication continued via node1 and node3
Restarted mariadb on node2, confirmed automatic IST resync to cluster_size=3, Synced, and recovery of the row written during its outage
Captured boot_id/uptime/cluster-health/data baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via 'systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled each until exec was available again
Verified changed boot_id on each node post-reboot
Verified mariadb auto-started, cluster rejoined at size 3 with Synced state, and test data intact on each node before proceeding to the next

evidence.requirement: Member automatically resynchronizes when it returns
evidence.summary: mariadb restarted on node2; it rejoins with wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and contains the row written while it was down (id=3, while-node2-down), proving automatic IST/SST resync
